title: The Quarry Document Archive
description: Ruth Cannady's companion to The Quarry, where the records she gets out of Verity County are posted whole, with the request date, the response date and the redactions marked.

data.author: Ruth Cannady
data.tagline: Requests, responses, packets, invoices and letters, with the dates on them.
data.about:
The documents behind [url=synth://thequarry.news/]The Quarry[/url], which is a letter that comes out once a month from Gridfall.

Everything here was obtained under the state public records act, handed across a counter, or picked up off the table by the door at a meeting, and every item says which. Every item has a note of two sentences on it saying what the document is. The note does not say what the document means.

Where something has been withheld the item says how many pages and reproduces the basis the agency gave, if it gave one.

Copies of anything: write and say which Q number. No form, no account, no charge. Start at [url=/post/how-this-works]how this is numbered[/url] or go to [url=/post/index-agencies]the index by agency[/url].

Ruth Cannady, Gridfall.

posts.title: How this is numbered, and what a note is
posts.body:
The letter is at [url=synth://thequarry.news/]thequarry.news[/url] and comes out once a month. This is where the paper goes.

[b]Numbering.[/b] Q-2025-01 onward, in the order I filed. It is mine and it means nothing to anybody else. Where the agency gave the request a number of its own it is printed beside mine, and if the two disagree the agency's is the one to quote at the agency.

[b]The note.[/b] Every item has a note of two sentences on it. The note says what the document is. It does not say what the document means, and if you want that it is in the letter or it is nowhere.

[b]Redactions.[/b] Where an agency has withheld something the item says how many pages and reproduces the basis it cited, if it cited one. Where I have taken something out myself it is marked [redacted by RC], and the reason is always a private person's name, address or telephone number that the agency left in by accident. Eleven times so far, never a public employee's name.

[b]Formats and copies.[/b] Most of what comes back is a scan with no text layer, which is a picture of text; where I have made a searchable version I say so and say it is mine and not the document. Write and say which Q number and it comes by email, or on a stick in the post if it is large. No form, no account, no charge.

[b]The form number, because everybody asks.[/b] A public records request in this county is [b]Form VC-5[/b] on the [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]services portal[/url], [b]Form VC-114[/b] across the [url=synth://verityclerk.gov/s/records-request]clerk's counter[/url], and [b]Form VC-9[/b] according to the transit division's own page. All three get filled. I use VC-114 because it is one step shorter, and the clerk's office says the same on its own site.

[b]The clock.[/b] Five business days to respond in writing, which is not the same as producing, and one extension, in writing, with a reason. Hand it over the counter and ask for the date stamp on your copy. It settles every argument about when the clock started.

[b]What this costs.[/b] The letter's hosting is nineteen dollars a month and this adds four for the storage. Records fees were four hundred and ten last year. Transcription errors go on [url=/post/corrections]the corrections page[/url], the item stays where it is with the correction on it, and nothing here has been taken down.

Ruth Cannady, Gridfall.

comments.author: mod_dcarver
comments.body: Three form numbers for one form. Somebody in that building knows which one is right and has retired.

comments.author: Ruth Cannady
comments.body: All three get filled. That is the part that surprised me.

posts.title: Commissioners' minutes, 17 June and 1 July 2003
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2025-19. Clerk's log 2025-044.[*]Filed 6 May 2025, Form VC-114, across the counter, date-stamped.[*]Response 13 May 2025. Filled. Five business days.[*]14 pages, under fifty, so no charge and no staff time.[*]No redactions.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] These are the minutes of the two regular meetings of the Verity County Board of Commissioners that followed the Substation No. 3 fire of 11 June 2003. A minute records who was there, what was moved, who seconded and how the vote went, and these ones do that.

[code]
VERITY COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS
Regular Meeting -- Tuesday, 17 June 2003, 6:00 p.m.
Courthouse, 14 Depot Street, Gridfall

PRESENT: Ostrand (chair), Nagy, Quillen, Reiter, Sowash.  ABSENT: none.

  7.  Report of the Emergency Management Coordinator on the outage
      of 11 June 2003. Coordinator Shultz reported. Received and
      placed on file.

  8.  Resolution 2003-31, thanking the Gridfall Volunteer Fire
      Company No. 1 and the Ashkettle Volunteer Fire Department for
      services rendered 11 June 2003. Moved Reiter, seconded Nagy.
      Adopted 5-0.

  9.  Claim, Depot Street Oil Co., generator fuel, courthouse and
      annex, 11-12 June 2003 .......................... $412.60
      Moved Sowash, seconded Quillen. Approved 5-0.

 12.  Communication, Verity Valley Power & Light, dated 13 June
      2003, read by the clerk. Company reports restoration complete
      except the Tannery Flats and Hollis Road circuits. Received
      and placed on file.

 14.  Moved Quillen, seconded Reiter, that the clerk write to Verity
      Valley Power & Light requesting a written report as to the
      cause of the failure at Substation No. 3. Carried 5-0.

 19.  Adjourned 7:41 p.m.
[/code]

[code]
Regular Meeting -- Tuesday, 1 July 2003, 6:00 p.m.
PRESENT: Ostrand (chair), Nagy, Quillen, Sowash.  ABSENT: Reiter.

  5.  Communication, Verity Valley Power & Light, 26 June 2003, in
      reply to the request of 17 June. Company states the cause is
      under investigation by the company and by the State Utility
      Commission and that no report will issue until that is
      complete. Received and placed on file.

  6.  Moved Nagy, seconded Quillen, that the clerk write to the
      State Utility Commission requesting a copy of its findings
      when issued. Carried 4-0.

 11.  Claim, Verity County Fair Association, exhibition hall
      opened as a cooling station 11 June ......... $186.00
      Approved 4-0.
[/code]

The commission's two-page summary is dated November 2003. There is no item in the minutes of 2003 or 2004 recording its receipt, and I have read all forty-seven meetings of those two years.

The Ledger's report of the fire, filed the same day, is at [url=synth://verityledger.com/article/fire-2003]verityledger.com[/url]. The wiki article is [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]here[/url].

comments.author: kfennimore
comments.body: The fuel claim is in the paper too. [b]Gridfall Ledger, 20 June 2003, page 5[/b], bottom of the second column, under the county proceedings, which the Ledger printed every fortnight until 2009 and which nobody has ever asked me for. It spells the coordinator Schultz, which is wrong, and which the minutes get right.

posts.title: An invoice for $18.15 and the corrected one for $10.65
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-05. County intake VC-5 no. 2026-0341.[*]Filed 3 February 2026. Response 24 February 2026, after one written extension.[*]121 pages. Invoice 2026-0488 issued with the response, corrected invoice 2026-0503 on 3 March.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] These are two invoices from Administrative Services for the same 121 pages, eight days apart. The first charges from page one and the second charges from page fifty-one.

[code]
VERITY COUNTY ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES
INVOICE 2026-0488                              24 February 2026

  Public records request VC-5 2026-0341
  Copies, 121 pages @ $0.15 ........................ $18.15
  Staff time, 25 minutes ............................ no charge
                                                     ------
  TOTAL DUE                                          $18.15
  Records will be released on payment.
[/code]

I sent back a copy of Resolution 2024-11 with Section 1 marked, and nothing else, on 25 February. Section 1 is two sentences:

[quote=Resolution 2024-11, adopted 5 December 2023]SECTION 1. Copies. No charge shall be made for the first fifty (50) pages of any single request. From the fifty-first page the charge shall be fifteen cents ($0.15) per page, without regard to paper size.[/quote]

[code]
INVOICE 2026-0503     (supersedes 2026-0488)       3 March 2026

  Public records request VC-5 2026-0341
  Copies, 121 pages, first 50 no charge
    71 pages @ $0.15 ................................ $10.65
  Staff time, 25 minutes ............................. no charge
                                                      ------
  TOTAL DUE                                           $10.65
  Invoice 2026-0488 is withdrawn.
[/code]

Seven dollars fifty. The covering letter apologises in one sentence and does not say how the first was worked out. I did not ask, because it was worked out by multiplying.

The clerk's fee page quotes the resolution by number: [url=synth://verityclerk.gov/s/fees]verityclerk.gov[/url]. The portal's records page gives fifteen cents a page and does not mention the first fifty: [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]verity.county.gov[/url]. Both are county pages. The full two-page resolution goes to anybody who asks for Q-2026-02.

comments.author: j_ruddock
comments.body: I paid $31.20 last year for 208 pages from the same office. Was that wrong too?

comments.author: Ruth Cannady
comments.body: 208 pages, first fifty free, 158 at fifteen cents is $23.70. You were charged from page one. Send them the invoice number and Section 1; they corrected mine in eight days.

posts.title: Table 4, five years of it
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-06. Not a county record and not a records request.[*]Asked for by email from the state utility commission's docket room, 18 November 2025. Sent the same week.[*]Five reports, 2021 through 2025, searchable as filed. No fee, no redactions.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] These are Table 4 of Verity Valley Power & Light's annual reliability reports to the state utility commission for 2021 through 2025, which is the table of sustained interruptions by circuit. The rows for the Pell Road lateral, circuit 4412-E, are reproduced below and the five full reports go to anybody who asks.

[code]
TABLE 4 -- SUSTAINED INTERRUPTIONS BY CIRCUIT (extract)
Circuit 4412-E  PELL ROAD LATERAL  (est. 404 meters)

YEAR   SUSTAINED   LONGEST     MEDIAN    CAUSE CODES GIVEN
2021       2       1h 05m      38 min    WX, UNK
2022       1       0h 47m      47 min    WX
2023       2       2h 12m      66 min    WX, EQ
2024       7       3h 18m      49 min    WX x3, EQ x3, UNK
2025       9       5h 40m      51 min    EQ x6, WX x2, UNK

Five of the seven 2024 interruptions fall after 30 June.
Fourteen in the eighteen months July 2024 to December 2025.
District average, laterals of comparable meter count, same
period: 3.

CAPITAL PLAN FILINGS -- 4412-E REBUILD
  filed 2023, scheduled 2024 ..... $1.1M   ~2.0 mi conductor
  filed 2024, scheduled 2025 ..... $1.1M   ~2.0 mi conductor
  filed 2025, scheduled 2027 ..... $1.1M   ~2.0 mi conductor
  Six weeks of work in each of the three filings.
[/code]

The company's narrative on the circuit, 2025 report, page 31, in full:

[quote=Verity Valley Power & Light, 2025 annual reliability report, p.31]Circuit 4412-E continues to exhibit recurrent faulting attributable to aged conductor. Rebuild is recommended. The work is carried in the capital plan.[/quote]

[b]Q-2026-06a, the company's statement.[/b] Two questions went to Verity Valley on 26 February 2026 and again, unchanged, on 5 March: what decided the three deferrals, in what order and with what weight, and whether anybody on the lateral was told at the time that the cause was a known conductor condition. The answer came on 13 March, eleven days after the second:

[quote=Verity Valley Power & Light]Reliability investment is prioritised annually across the service territory based on a range of factors, including customer impact, asset condition and system need. We do not comment on individual circuits.[/quote]

That is the answer to both. I have not asked a third time.

Nothing on this page is a county record. Verity Valley is a company and the act does not reach it; these are its filings with the state, and the state's docket room sends them to anybody who writes, for nothing.

The letter is [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-76]here[/url]. The company's announcements are at [url=synth://vvpl.news/]vvpl.news[/url]. The same question was asked on [url=synth://askverity.com/q/q-11]AskVerity[/url] in January and got an answer about circuit breakers.

comments.author: wpennock
comments.body: Cause code EQ is equipment, WX is weather, UNK is undetermined. Six EQ in one year on one lateral is the company telling the state what it is. Thirty-four years and I never saw that table until you put it up.

posts.title: The 2014 trail conveyance, the paragraph everybody argues about
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-09. A recorded instrument, so no request and no clock.[*]Counter copy, clerk's office, 5 May 2026. 6 pages at twenty-five cents, plain, not certified ... $1.50[*]Instrument 2014-0043371, recorded 19 September 2014. No redactions.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] This is the deed by which the former Verity Rail branch corridor passed to Verity County in 2014, and the paragraph below is the whole of the description of what was conveyed. The word bridge does not appear in the instrument and neither does the word trestle.

[code]
INSTRUMENT 2014-0043371
Recorded 19 September 2014, 11:04 a.m., Office of the County Clerk

  ... TOGETHER WITH all right, title and interest of the Grantor in
  and to the roadbed, ballast, sub-ballast, embankments, cuts,
  fills, culverts, drainage structures, fencing and appurtenances
  lying within the corridor above described, and all rights of way
  appurtenant thereto;

  EXCEPTING AND RESERVING to the Grantor all signal apparatus,
  communication lines, poles and attachments thereto, together with
  a right of entry for the removal of the same for a period of
  twenty-four (24) months from the date hereof;

  SUBJECT TO all easements, leases, licenses and crossing
  agreements of record ...
[/code]

Culverts and drainage structures are conveyed. Signals and communication lines are reserved. Bridges are in neither list.

Three of the four structures on the branch were decked over when the trail opened in 2014. The fourth is at Coyne Creek and has been fenced since that autumn. The parks department says the structure was excluded from the conveyance; the recorded instrument neither excludes it nor includes it. Both sentences are true at once.

The letter is [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-79]here[/url]. The county wiki's account of the abandonment is better sourced than anything the county has published: [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/verity-rail]wiki.gridfall.net[/url]. The right-of-way page is [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/rail-crossing]here[/url] and has said under review since 2019.

comments.author: kfennimore
comments.body: The 1889 conveyance the original right of way came out of is quoted in a 1923 exchange in the Ledger, [b]12 and 19 June 1923, page 4[/b], in an argument about a fence and a mule. Four lines of it, and it settles nothing either. Ninety-one years apart and both instruments are silent about the same things.

comments.author: r_teasdale
comments.body: so who fixes the bridge

comments.author: Ruth Cannady
comments.body: Nobody has since 2014 and each office says it is the other one. The fence has been replaced once, in 2021, and that invoice is [url=/post/trestle-fence-invoice-2021]here[/url].

posts.title: Packet page 3 and packet page 11
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-13. No number from the board, which does not number them.[*]Packet collected at the meeting of 8 April 2026, free, off the table by the door.[*]2 pages of a 24-page packet, reproduced whole. No redactions.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] These are two pages of the same Ashkettle Water Board packet for the meeting of 8 April 2026. Page three records the award of the rate study and page eleven records an addendum to it approved in November 2025.

[code]
PACKET, 8 APRIL 2026 -- PAGE 3

  6. RATE STUDY -- RECEIPT OF FINAL REPORT
     Award history: contract awarded 14 June 2023 to Tarn
     Engineering, Ridgemont, in the amount of $41,000 for a
     cost-of-service and rate study of the district.
     Final report delivered 4 March 2026.
     Recommendation: 9 percent increase, phased over three years.

PACKET, 8 APRIL 2026 -- PAGE 11

  APPENDIX B -- CONTRACT AMENDMENTS, CURRENT BIENNIUM
    Tarn Engineering, rate study, Amendment 1:
      additional hydraulic modelling, east pressure zone,
      approved 12 November 2025 ................... $9,800
    Total contract as amended ...................... $50,800
[/code]

Fifty thousand eight hundred dollars. I read page three in April and wrote $41,000 in the letter, and I did not read page eleven until June.

The letter that had it wrong is [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-77]here[/url], unaltered. The correction is [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-79]here[/url]. A summary account published $38,000 in between, and there is no $38,000 in any document about this study, which I put here because this is the page a person checking it will reach.

The board's minutes and agendas are at [url=synth://veritywater.org/s/minutes-archive]veritywater.org[/url].

comments.author: a_dunnet
comments.body: The addendum was on the November agenda as Appendix B as well, and it was voted on, and it took four minutes. I am not saying that to be unkind. Four minutes is what an appendix gets.

posts.title: The 8 April agenda and the 8 April minutes
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-14. Both collected rather than requested.[*]Agenda from the packet, 8 April 2026. Minutes approved 13 May 2026 and collected that evening.[*]2 pages. No charge, no redactions.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] This is page two of the printed agenda for the Ashkettle Water Board meeting of 8 April 2026 and page three of the approved minutes of the same meeting. The agenda names Halvey as the mover on item 6 and the minutes name Trewin, with Halvey seconding.

[code]
AGENDA -- ASHKETTLE WATER BOARD -- 8 APRIL 2026 -- p.2

  6. Rate study, receipt of final report.
     Motion: Trustee Halvey. Second: Trustee Trewin.
     Action requested: receive and file.

MINUTES -- 8 APRIL 2026 -- p.3   (approved 13 May 2026)

  6. Rate study, receipt of final report.
     Trustee Trewin moved that the report be received and filed.
     Trustee Halvey seconded.
     Discussion: Trustee Dunnet spoke against receiving the report
       without a separate motion on the phase-in.
     Roll call: Halvey aye. Trewin aye. Prosser aye. Mahaffey aye.
       Dunnet no.   Carried 4-1.
[/code]

An agenda is written before a meeting and a minute is written after one. Where they differ the minute is the record, and the minute is the document nobody prints.

I took the mover off the agenda. The correction is in [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-79]the June letter[/url] with what I did about it.

The clerk of the board has changed the copy of the agenda on the board's site. The copy that went out in the packet is the one above and there is no mechanism for changing that one. The board's page is [url=synth://veritywater.org/s/minutes-archive]here[/url].

comments.author: mod_dcarver
comments.body: Every board in this county prints the mover on the agenda before the mover has moved anything. It is not a lie, it is a plan, and then somebody files the plan.

posts.title: The Ridgemont dispatch contract, 61 pages of 74
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-07. County intake VC-5 no. 2026-0188.[*]Filed 12 May 2026, in person, date-stamped. Acknowledged 19 May, five business days.[*]Extension 2 June 2026, in writing, reason given: review by the authority's counsel.[*]Response 9 July 2026. 61 pages released of 74. 13 withheld in full, 3 of the released pages redacted in part.[*]11 pages over the first fifty @ $0.15 ... $1.65. Staff time 45 min, 15 chargeable @ $31/hr ... $7.75. Paid $9.40.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] This is the Interlocal Communications Services Agreement between Verity County and the Ridgemont three-county communications authority, adopted 3 March 2026 and effective 1 September 2026. Thirteen of the seventy-four pages were withheld in full, three more came with lines taken out, and the county's own redaction log is reproduced below.

[code]
REDACTION LOG -- VC-5 2026-0188 -- 9 JULY 2026

PAGE(S)  WITHHELD                        BASIS CITED
11       Sec. 9.2, lines 4-9             s.87(2)(d) commercial
12       Sec. 9.3, in full               s.87(2)(d) commercial
13       Sec. 9.4, table, in full        s.87(2)(d) commercial
29       Sec. 12.1, lines 11-14          s.87(2)(d) commercial
41-51    Exhibit C, pricing schedule     s.87(2)(d) commercial
52       Sec. 14.6, lines 1-3            -- none given --

Withheld in full 13. Released with lines out 3. Released 61.
[/code]

The clerk's office publishes the rule that a refusal names the exemption by section. One line of this log does not. I asked for a corrected log on 13 July and have not had one; when it comes it goes on this page under the old one.

[b]From the released pages.[/b] Section 6.4, not redacted, in full:

[quote=Interlocal Communications Services Agreement, s.6.4]The Authority shall answer ninety (90) percent of emergency calls within fifteen (15) seconds and ninety-five (95) percent within twenty (20) seconds, such performance to be measured monthly across all served jurisdictions in the aggregate and not by jurisdiction.[/quote]

Section 3.1, term: five years from 1 September 2026, opt-out at the end of year three on payment of the balance remaining. Section 11.2, excluded: the non-emergency line, animal control, after-hours highway calls and the road department callout list. Exhibit A: sixteen positions, of which the authority undertakes to staff "not fewer than four" at all hours. Exhibit B: cutover 1 September, parallel operation for the fourteen days before it, and a joint test of the road-name database in July, which I have asked whether anybody ran.

Signature page: signed for the county by the administrator on 4 March 2026. Adopted by the board the day before, on the consent agenda, item 14 of 19, in a block, without discussion.

The letter is [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-78]here[/url]. The sheriff's page on what changed is [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/dispatch]here[/url].

posts.title: The Form VC-63 log
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-20. County intake VC-5 no. 2026-0771.[*]Filed 21 July 2026. Response 28 July 2026, five business days.[*]6 pages, released whole. No charge.[*]Names and street addresses of reporting parties redacted by the county. Town retained.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] This is the county's log of interference reports filed on Form VC-63 for the Route 62 corridor between January 2024 and June 2026, thirty-one entries, forwarded quarterly to the Office of Emergency Management. The county's cover letter states that it holds no inspection, measurement or investigation record responsive to the request.

Eight entries below, as printed. The other twenty-three are in the file.

[code]
FORM VC-63 INTERFERENCE REPORT LOG -- ROUTE 62 CORRIDOR

NO  RECD        OBSERVED     LOCATION AS GIVEN      FREQ AS GIVEN
03  2024-02-11  02/09 eve    Ashkettle              "TV channel 7"
07  2024-05-02  04/28        Kestrel Rd, Ashkettle  "AM 1340"
11  2024-08-19  08/17 night  quarry overlook        4.219
14  2024-11-06  11/02        Ashkettle              "garage door"
19  2025-03-24  03/21 23:07  Rt 62 e. of Ashkettle  42.19
22  2025-07-08  07/05 01:07  Rt 62, milepost 9      4219 kHz
26  2026-01-15  01/13 eve    Coyne Flats            "the LED sign"
31  2026-06-02  05/30        Ashkettle              unknown

Name and street address redacted on every entry. Frequencies are
printed as the reporting party wrote them and are not normalised.
Forwarded 2024 Q1-Q4, 2025 Q1-Q4, 2026 Q1-Q2, all acknowledged.
[/code]

The cover letter, in full:

[quote=Verity County Administrative Services, 28 July 2026]Enclosed is the interference report log for the period requested, with the names and street addresses of reporting parties withheld under s.87(2)(b). The County holds no inspection report, measurement record, investigation file or correspondence with any federal or state agency responsive to the remainder of your request. The County does not operate a transmitter at the location described in the majority of these reports and holds no record identifying an operator.[/quote]

The intake form is Form VC-63 and the service page is [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/route62-signal]here[/url].

comments.author: wpennock
comments.body:
Entry 19 gives 42.19 and entry 22 gives 4219 kHz. Those are not the same number and neither is what entry 11 gives. One of them is a decimal point that did not survive being typed into a box and then typed again out of it; which one I could not tell you.

I filed a VC-63 in 2024. The field is five hundred characters and mine did not fit, so what went in was the first three lines. That is on the form and not on the county.

posts.title: Twenty-eight pages of the 16 September schools packet
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-26. District reference PRR-2026-14.[*]Filed 11 September 2026 by email. Response 15 September 2026, two business days.[*]28 pages released of the 61-page agenda packet. Fee waived by the district.[*]The 34-page operator's proposal was not part of this request and is at the district office counter.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] These are twenty-eight pages of the agenda packet for the Verity County School District board meeting of Wednesday 16 September 2026, at which the board voted 4 to 3 to contract the bus runs. The pages are the agenda, Resolution 2026-11, the business administrator's cost comparison, the bid tabulation and the fuel escalator page.

The comparison is the page that does the work and it is reproduced whole:

[code]
BUSINESS ADMINISTRATOR'S COST COMPARISON -- 16 SEPT 2026 -- p.2
Five-year pupil transportation cost, both methods

                     IN HOUSE      CONTRACT      CONTRACT
                                  (operator's   (district's
                                   figure)       figure)
  Year 1            $  612,000    $  580,000    $  580,000
  Year 2            $  630,400    $  580,000    $  597,400
  Year 3            $  649,300    $  580,000    $  615,300
  Year 4            $  668,800    $  580,000    $  633,800
  Year 5            $  688,900    $  580,000    $  652,800
                    ----------    ----------    ----------
  FIVE-YEAR TOTAL   $3,249,400    $2,900,000    $3,079,300

  Note: the operator quotes a flat annual price. The district's
  column applies the fuel escalator at Section 7.4 of the
  proposal, which is three percent a year and is not optional.
[/code]

Both columns were in the packet. The figure read into the record at the meeting was $2.9 million.

Resolution 2026-11 is two pages and the award is one sentence of them. The roll call is on page two: ayes Ulm, Sipes, Yost, Deitz; noes Corry, Hannigan, Strunk. Taken at 10:02 p.m., after eleven speakers.

The district's own account of what changes on 4 January is at [url=synth://verityschools.org/s/bus-contract]verityschools.org[/url] and is, page for page, the clearest thing any county body has published this year. It raised no objection to these pages going up and said it saved them the copying.

The wire filing from the room is at [url=synth://veritywire.press/d/d-401]veritywire.press[/url]. Hal Brenner has the arithmetic in [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/]his notebook[/url] and it is the packet's, which is the right one.

comments.author: l_corry
comments.body: The column on the right is the one I asked to be read out and it was not read out. I am not saying anybody hid it. It was in the packet, it was on page two, and the number that left the room was the other one.

posts.title: The ambulance billing contract, refused twice
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2026-24. County intake VC-5 no. 2026-0902.[*]Filed 2 September 2026, in person, date-stamped.[*]Refused in writing 9 September 2026, five business days. Refused again by telephone 15 September.[*]Appeal to the county administrator posted 16 September 2026.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] These are the two refusals of my request for the county's ambulance billing services agreement, which was renewed in 2024 by administrative signature. The first is a letter that names no exemption and the second is a telephone call that I wrote up the same afternoon and read back.

As filed:

[code]
FORM VC-5, 2 September 2026
  The agreement for ambulance billing services between Verity
  County and its billing vendor, as renewed in calendar year 2024,
  together with the instrument of renewal and any delegation of
  authority relied upon in signing it.
[/code]

The letter of 9 September, in full:

[quote=Verity County Administrative Services]Your request of 2 September is denied. The agreement you describe is an agreement with a private vendor and is not a public document of the County.[/quote]

No section is cited. The clerk's office publishes on its own site that a refusal names the exemption it relies on by section.

The memorandum, which is my document and not the county's:

[code]
MEMORANDUM OF TELEPHONE CALL
15 September 2026, 2:18 p.m., 14 minutes.
R. Cannady to Administrative Services, records line.

  I asked which section the refusal of 9 September relied on. I
  was told the agreement is the vendor's and not the county's,
  and that this is not an exemption question because there is no
  county record to exempt.

  I asked whether the county holds a signed copy. Yes, in the
  finance office.

  I asked whether a signed copy held in the finance office is a
  record of the county. I was told that would have to be looked
  at.

  Read back at 2:31 p.m. and agreed accurate. I did not ask for
  and was not given a name.
[/code]

And the third document, which I did get, from the clerk, for nothing:

[code]
RESOLUTION 2019-22 (extract)
  SECTION 2. The County Administrator is authorised to execute
  renewals of existing service agreements without further action
  of the Board where the annual consideration does not exceed
  the threshold in Section 3 and the term does not exceed three
  (3) years.

  SECTION 4. Every renewal executed under Section 2 shall be
  reported to the Board at its next regular meeting and shall be
  entered in the minutes.
[/code]

Section 4 is why I filed. I have read the minutes of every regular meeting of 2024. There is one line: [i]Renewals executed under Resolution 2019-22 reported. Received and placed on file.[/i] It does not say what was renewed.

The appeal went in the post on 16 September. Under the act it goes to the county administrator, which is the office that signed the renewal. I am not complaining about that, I am telling you where the letter went.

Open. It gets an update on this page when there is one.

comments.author: n_ferriday
comments.body: I got an ambulance bill in March with a second company's name on it and a different address for payment and I assumed it was a scam. It was not a scam.

comments.author: Ruth Cannady
comments.body: That is the vendor. If you still have the bill, keep it; the date on it is useful and I will not print your name.

posts.title: Corrections to this archive
posts.body:
Transcription errors, tagging errors and my own arithmetic. The item stays where it is with the correction on it. Nothing here has been taken down.

[b]2 June 2026.[/b] The transcription of instrument 2014-0043371 gave the number as 2014-0043317. Two digits transposed, by me, typing. The scan was always right.

[b]18 June 2026.[/b] The fence invoice item said the sign was 24 by 18 inches. The specification sheet says 18 by 24. It is a portrait sign and I wrote it as landscape.

[b]14 August 2026.[/b] The invoice item gave the difference between the two invoices as $7.35. It is $7.50. 121 pages less the first fifty is 71 pages, at fifteen cents, is $10.65, against $18.15. Subtraction.

[b]1 September 2026.[/b] The Table 4 item was tagged [i]county-clerk[/i] for five months. It is not a county record at all. Retagged.

[b]9 September 2026.[/b] The dispatch contract item said 62 pages were released. It is 61. The redaction log says 61 and so does the cover letter and I typed 62 twice.

If you find another one, write and say which item and which line. Four people have done that and all four were right.

comments.author: kfennimore
comments.body: Five corrections in seventeen months, all of them yours, all found and posted. The Ledger's page has two thousand and eleven and a quarter of them say a machine did something.

comments.author: Ruth Cannady
comments.body: Mine are easier. There are sixteen items on this site and there is one of me.

posts.title: Q-2025-11 is still open
posts.body:
[list][*]Q-2025-11. County intake VC-5 no. 2025-0417.[*]Filed [b]14 July 2025[/b], in person, date-stamped.[*]Acknowledged 21 July 2025, within the five days. Estimate given: approximately thirty days.[*]Extension 26 August 2025, in writing, reason given: volume and the need to consult another office.[*]Nothing since. Fourteen months on Monday 14 September 2026. Ten follow-ups.[/list]

[b]Note.[/b] This is a request to Administrative Services for correspondence with the Office of County Counsel about the county's parcel file for the Substation No. 3 site, and for any record naming the office that holds that file. It has been open since 14 July 2025 and nothing responsive has been produced.

[code]
FORM VC-5, 14 July 2025

  1. Correspondence between Administrative Services and the Office
     of County Counsel, 1 January 2018 to the date of this request,
     concerning the county's parcel file for the Substation No. 3
     site at Depot and Quarry Road, Gridfall.

  2. Any record identifying the office that is custodian of that
     file.

  Received at the counter 14 July 2025, stamped.
[/code]

[b]The follow-ups, all ten.[/b]

[code]
  1.  30 Sept 2025  telephone  Told it was with counsel.
  2.  21 Oct 2025   email      No reply.
  3.  18 Nov 2025   letter     Over the counter, date-stamped.
  4.  16 Dec 2025   telephone  Told the records officer had left
                               and the post was vacant.
  5.  27 Jan 2026   email      To the county administrator.
                               Acknowledged same day.
  6.  10 Mar 2026   telephone  Told it was on a list.
  7.  28 Apr 2026   email      No reply.
  8.  16 Jun 2026   telephone  Told the file was being located.
  9.  4 Aug 2026    letter     Date-stamped, with the 2025
                               acknowledgement attached.
 10.  2 Sept 2026   email      Automatic acknowledgement returned.
[/code]

That acknowledgement, as it arrived on 2 September 2026:

[quote=Verity County mail system]Your request {{request_type}} has been received by {{agency_name}} and will be processed within {{sla_days}} business days.[/quote]

The clerk's office has reported that acknowledgement twice and says so on its own [url=synth://verityclerk.gov/s/records-log]records log[/url]. The letter that office sends by post is written by a person and says five days.

[b]What this is about, so nobody has to guess.[/b] The county's [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/substation-parcel]service page for the parcel[/url] has said [i]temporarily unavailable while records are transferred to the new system[/i] since 6 November 2019, and Form VC-77 with it. That page directs inquiries to the Office of County Counsel. The Office of County Counsel directs parcel inquiries to that page. Residents have been documenting that loop on [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]the old boards[/url] for years. I asked which office holds the file. That is the whole question.

It is not a question about the fire. The fire was on 11 June 2003, the commission published its two-page summary in November 2003, and that file is the commission's and not the county's.

[b]I have not appealed.[/b] Under the act the appeal goes to the county administrator, and I have written to that office twice in the ordinary way and both times it acknowledged and nothing moved. I will file at fifteen months if the fifteenth month looks like the fourteenth.

comments.author: mod_dcarver
comments.body: The loop has been on the boards since 2019. Somebody posts the letter from Counsel, somebody posts the page, and then it stops, because that is where it stops.

comments.author: wpennock
comments.body: Nothing in a parcel file would tell you anything about that morning. The yard at Depot and Quarry Road was rebuilt in 2015, unmanned, run by SCADA from two states away, and there is no crew room in it. I drove out for the ribbon cutting. The file is a file.

Seven lines for nineteen things, because the rest are one folder each and there is nothing to say about them.
